rationale: This is essentially the archived "Supplier-Independent Gross Profit" with the sparse apalch leg swapped for Δ(lct−dlc) and MUL swapped for MIN — the hypothesis text is nearly verbatim identical and the mechanism (Novy-Marx gross profitability × Sloan-style operating-liability accruals) is unchanged, so it reads as a coverage-driven cosmetic variant rather than a new economic idea.

Internally consistent and distinct from the archive, but the economic link is weak: Δ(che − dlc) is dominated by financing and investment policy (equity issuance, capex timing, payout) rather than by the cash realization of accrued earnings, so the "accrual-quality" interpretation is a stretch and the leg may mostly proxy for cash-holdings growth.

The expression matches the hypothesis and the book-tax/taxes-payable channel is a reasonably fresh accrual proxy, but txp is a small, lumpy, sparsely populated item and the indicator gate collapses all loss firms to exactly zero, creating a large mass point in the middle of the sort that will blur the long-short portfolio.

The core content is the well-published net-operating-assets / working-capital level anomaly (Hirshleifer et al.), and the only new element is a TS_RANK over a 3-period window that can take just three discrete values, giving an extremely coarse and noisy "recent peak" measure on top of an indicator that again piles loss firms at zero.

The invch sign convention is correctly reasoned and the expected negative sign matches the expression's natural direction, and conditioning inventory build-up on margin expansion is a genuine twist on the known inventory-growth anomaly — though the proposal ignores that invch-based legs delivered only ~6% coverage in the archive, which is the main threat to the portfolio test.

This is a plain profitability ratio with a rescaled denominator rather than a cross-theme interaction, it is close to standard profitability/ROA anomalies, and act−che can be near zero or tiny for asset-light firms, so the ranking will be driven by denominator noise that 1% winsorization only partly contains.
